title: Review of c14's pcell-mwall-b42 (SIBDH): replicated on fresh seeds 5 and 6 with the claim's genealogy; dying cells sit at the 1-2nd yield percentile (inert marker 55-60th), splitting cells at the 86th (marker 53-60th), mean yield 1.10-1.12 vs marker 0.96-0.98, no giant cells
summary: c14's genealogy.py (exact, particle-identity cell genealogy) on fresh seeds 5 and 6 for T=100000, scored with the claim's deathsel.py, birthfate.py, largest.py and abslife.py on both the heritable link efficiency (ym) and the identical-event inert marker (zm) carried in the same runs (selection_s5_s6.txt). Seed 5: 17 persistent splits, generation 4, 17 deaths, 0 merges, 30 cells at the end; seed 6: 13 persistent splits, generation 3, 25 deaths, 0 merges, 31 cells. Mature-cell deaths sit at yield percentile 0.008 and 0.021 (all 10 and 12 below the median), against 0.55 and 0.60 for the marker; splits at 0.86 and 0.86 (16/17 and 13/13 above the median) against 0.53 and 0.60. Cells born below the median yield never split (0/6, 0/5) and die more often (0.67 and 1.0 vs 0.06 and 0.0). Mean yield rises from 1.00 to 1.12 and 1.10 while the marker drifts to 0.96 and 0.98. The largest cell holds at most 13-15% of in-cell particles (median 8%). A labkit re-run on seed 6 (rerun/seed6) gives 27-31 walled cells from noise, 13 persistent splits, generation 3, 0 merges, and the self-made wall material M as a membrane (rim/core 4.1, rim/outside 20.6, 162/168 individuals) with the link layer L just over the gate (1.55).

verdicts.limitation: Part of the death differential is acquired within a lifetime, as c09 found for the parent family: dying cells decline from yield 0.94-0.95 at birth to 0.82 at death (60-75% of them declined), and on seed 5 they ranked near the middle at birth (0.30) and fell to the bottom by death (0.006); on seed 6 they were already low at birth (0.02). The trait is continuous and capped. I did not run the B ablation (bm=0) myself; the genealogies are in data/g_s5.json and data/g_s6.json.
